exposure: PFD group vs. control group (benign diseases)
Natural labor vs. cesarean birth within the PFD group
outcome: Morphological features of pelvic floor assessed by 3D ultrasound
Size and area of pelvic diaphragm
cohort: 40 women with pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) and 20 women with benign diseases as controls
finding: 3D ultrasound effectively revealed distinct morphological differences in the pelvic floor of women with PFD compared to controls, including organ prolapse, larger diaphragm size and area, and thinner puborectalis muscle, with some variations observed between natural labor and cesarean birth subgroups.
mod_finding: Women with PFD who had a natural delivery showed better pelvic floor muscle indicators (diaphragm diameter and area, thickness of musculi levator ani) compared to those who underwent a cesarean birth.
